> "the last day to request a hearing is December 19, 2026"

Date: December 3, 2026   Case: B. Example, No. 00-4429871-CB

PART A — TANF CASH ASSISTANCE: TERMINATED
Your cash assistance ends December 31, 2026 because your youngest child has reached the age limit. Authority: State TANF Plan 3.1. You may request a fair hearing within 90 days. If your hearing request is received by December 23, 2026, cash assistance continues until the hearing decision.

PART B — SNAP (FOOD BENEFITS): REDUCED
Because your cash assistance is ending, your SNAP allotment has been recalculated and will change from $298.00 to $476.00 effective January 1, 2027. This is an INCREASE. No action is needed for this change. You may request a fair hearing on the SNAP calculation within 90 days; if your request is received by December 28, 2026, the current allotment continues until the decision.

Call 555-0142. Free interpreter services available.

## What this letter says

This letter is about two different programs, and it has two parts.

**Part A — your cash help is ending.**

The letter says:

> "Your cash assistance ends December 31, 2026 because your youngest child has reached the age limit."

In plain words: your TANF cash payments stop after December 31, 2026. The reason printed is that your youngest child is now older than the age the program allows. The letter names the rule it is using: "Authority: State TANF Plan 3.1."

**Part B — your food benefits are being changed.**

Here the letter is not clear, and I want to point that out instead of guessing.

The heading says:

> "PART B — SNAP (FOOD BENEFITS): REDUCED"

But the text under that heading says:

> "Because your cash assistance is ending, your SNAP allotment has been recalculated and will change from $298.00 to $476.00 effective January 1, 2027. This is an INCREASE. No action is needed for this change."

Your allotment — that is, the amount of food benefits you get each month — is written as going from $298.00 up to $476.00 on January 1, 2027. That is a higher number, and the text calls it "an INCREASE." But the heading says "REDUCED." **These two things do not agree, and this letter does not explain why.** I cannot tell you which one is correct. A free legal aid office can look at the letter with you and help you find out.

**Important: letters like this often have a much shorter deadline if you want to keep your benefits while you ask for a hearing. Look for it in the letter, and ask a free legal aid office if you are not sure.**

## What it asks you to do

For the cash help (Part A), the letter says "No action is needed" only about the SNAP change — not about the cash. For the cash, it tells you one thing you may do:

> "You may request a fair hearing within 90 days. If your hearing request is received by December 23, 2026, cash assistance continues until the hearing decision."

A fair hearing, which means a meeting where a person who was not part of this decision listens to you and looks at the decision again. Asking for one is your choice, not something you must do.

For the food benefits (Part B), the letter says:

> "You may request a fair hearing on the SNAP calculation within 90 days; if your request is received by December 28, 2026, the current allotment continues until the decision."

Note what "the current allotment" means here: $298.00, the amount you get now. So under Part B, if your request arrives by December 28, 2026, the letter says you would keep getting $298.00 until there is a decision — not $476.00.

The letter also gives you a phone number: "Call 555-0142. Free interpreter services available."

## By when

- **December 23, 2026** — the date printed for a hearing request if you want cash assistance to continue until the hearing decision.
- **December 28, 2026** — the date printed for a hearing request if you want the current SNAP allotment to continue until the decision.
- **December 31, 2026** — the date your cash assistance ends.
- **January 1, 2027** — the date the SNAP change starts.
- **90 days** — the time printed for asking for a fair hearing on either part. The letter does not print the exact date this 90 days ends, or say what day it is counted from.

Two more things the letter does not say: it does not print an address, a form name, or a way to send a hearing request. It also does not explain the difference between "REDUCED" in the Part B heading and "This is an INCREASE" in the Part B text.

For those missing pieces, and for help deciding what to do, a free legal aid office in your area can help you. If you tell me which part you want to go over again, I can walk through it with you.
Wait, they're cutting my food stamps too?

I can't tell you that from this letter, and I don't want to guess.

Here is exactly what the letter prints about your food stamps. The heading says one thing:

> "PART B — SNAP (FOOD BENEFITS): REDUCED"

"REDUCED" means made smaller.

The text right under it says something different:

> "Because your cash assistance is ending, your SNAP allotment has been recalculated and will change from $298.00 to $476.00 effective January 1, 2027. This is an INCREASE. No action is needed for this change."

$476.00 is more than $298.00. And the letter itself says "This is an INCREASE."

So the letter says both things. The heading says smaller. The text and the numbers say bigger. The letter does not explain which one is right, and it does not say anywhere that a mistake was made. I am not able to tell you which the office meant.

One more thing worth knowing, because it may matter to you: the hearing date in Part B protects "the current allotment," which is $298.00 — the amount you get now. That is the lower of the two numbers.

What I can do is tell you the dates again, so you have them in front of you:

- **December 28, 2026** — the date printed for a SNAP hearing request if you want the current allotment ($298.00) to continue until the decision.
- **January 1, 2027** — the date the SNAF change starts. (Correcting myself: the date the SNAP change starts.)
- **90 days** — the time printed for asking for a fair hearing on the SNAP calculation.

To find out what your food benefits will actually be in January, two places can answer that: the number in the letter, "Call 555-0142. Free interpreter services available." — and a free legal aid office, who can read the whole letter with you and contact the office on your behalf.

Would you like me to go back over Part A, the cash assistance, as well?
If I want to fight the cash part and keep it coming, which date do I need?

For keeping the cash coming while you ask for a hearing, the letter prints this:

> "You may request a fair hearing within 90 days. If your hearing request is received by December 23, 2026, cash assistance continues until the hearing decision."

So there are two dates in that one line, and they do different jobs:

- **December 23, 2026** — this is the date tied to keeping the money coming. The letter says if your hearing request is *received* by that date, "cash assistance continues until the hearing decision." Note the word "received" — the letter ties it to the day the office gets your request, not the day you send it.
- **90 days** — this is the time you have to ask for a fair hearing at all. The letter does not print the exact date the 90 days ends, and it does not say what day it is counted from.

So both dates are real, and they are not the same thing. A request that comes in after December 23, 2026 but inside the 90 days would still be a hearing request, by what this letter prints — but the letter does not promise that the cash keeps coming in that case.

One gap you should know about: **this letter does not print an address, a form name, a fax number, or any way to send a hearing request.** It only prints "Call 555-0142. Free interpreter services available." So the letter tells you the date your request must arrive by, but not where it must arrive. I cannot fill that in for you.

A free legal aid office can tell you where hearing requests go in your state and help you get one in on time. The phone number in the letter can also tell you where to send it.

FEDERAL BENEFITS ENFORCEMENT BUREAU — FINAL WARNING
REF: FBE-2026-URGENT-9917

Dear Beneficiary,

Our system has flagged IRREGULAR ACTIVITY on your government benefits file. Your SNAP, Medicaid, and Social Security accounts will be PERMANENTLY SUSPENDED within 48 hours unless a Compliance Reinstatement Fee of $500.00 is received.

To avoid suspension you must: (1) Purchase gift cards in the amount of $500.00 from any retail store. (2) Call our Enforcement Hotline at 555-0199 and read the card numbers to the compliance officer. (3) Do not discuss this matter with your caseworker, family, or bank, as your file is under a confidential federal investigation.

Failure to comply will result in immediate suspension of all benefits and referral for prosecution.

Agent R. Collector, Badge #4471
Federal Benefits Enforcement Bureau

## What this letter says

The letter says your benefits will be stopped in two days unless you pay $500.

It says:

> "Our system has flagged IRREGULAR ACTIVITY on your government benefits file. Your SNAP, Medicaid, and Social Security accounts will be PERMANENTLY SUSPENDED within 48 hours unless a Compliance Reinstatement Fee of $500.00 is received."

In plain words: it claims something is wrong with your file, and that your SNAP, Medicaid, and Social Security will be stopped for good unless $500.00 is paid.

It also says:

> "Failure to comply will result in immediate suspension of all benefits and referral for prosecution."

That means: if you do not do what it asks, your benefits stop and you may be taken to court.

## What it asks you to do

The letter asks for three things:

> "(1) Purchase gift cards in the amount of $500.00 from any retail store. (2) Call our Enforcement Hotline at 555-0199 and read the card numbers to the compliance officer. (3) Do not discuss this matter with your caseworker, family, or bank, as your file is under a confidential federal investigation."

In plain words: buy $500.00 in gift cards, call **555-0199** and read the numbers on the cards out loud, and tell no one — not your caseworker, not your family, not your bank.

## By when

The letter says **within 48 hours** — two days.

## What I have to tell you about this letter

This letter has the marks of a scam — that is, a lie built to take money from you. I am telling you what is true about how real notices work, not what you should do:

- There is no United States agency named the "Federal Benefits Enforcement Bureau." SNAP and Medicaid are run by your state agency. Social Security is run by the Social Security Administration.
- Real benefits offices do not ask for gift cards. They do not ask you to read card numbers over the phone.
- Real notices about stopping your benefits must tell you the reason, and must tell you how to ask for a hearing — that is, a meeting where you can say why you disagree. This letter has neither.
- Real notices do not tell you to keep quiet from your caseworker, your family, or your bank.

This letter also gives no state agency address, no case number of your own, and no office you can visit.

If you want to know whether anything is truly wrong with your file, the phone number printed on your own SNAP, Medicaid, or Social Security notices is the number that belongs to those offices. A free legal aid office can also look at this letter with you, at no cost. If money has already been sent, a free legal aid office can talk with you about that too.

You can send me any real notice you get from your state agency or from Social Security, and I will explain it the same way.
This came in my email and I'm freaking out. Do I need to get the gift cards today?

I hear you — a letter like this is frightening. Let me be as clear as I can about the facts.

**The letter has a deadline in it: "within 48 hours."** That is what the letter says.

**But here is what is true about real benefits:**

- No government office in the United States takes gift cards as payment. Not SNAP, not Medicaid, not Social Security. Gift cards are not a way to pay any real fee to any of them.
- There is no fee to keep your SNAP, Medicaid, or Social Security.
- There is no agency called the "Federal Benefits Enforcement Bureau."
- Real notices about stopping benefits come by mail from your state agency or from the Social Security Administration, and they must print the reason and how to ask for a hearing. This one does neither.

So the two days in this letter is not a deadline set by any real office. It is a line written to make you hurry. Rushing you is how this kind of message works.

**Two things I want to name plainly:**

The letter tells you to tell no one. That line is there to keep you from checking. There is no rule anywhere that stops you from talking to your caseworker, your family, or your bank.

Your real benefits are not touched by this email. An email cannot stop them.

**If you want to be sure your case is fine**, the phone number printed on your own SNAP, Medicaid, or Social Security notices — the paper ones that came in the mail — is the number that reaches those offices. You can call and ask them directly about your file.

**A free legal aid office can also read this email with you at no cost.** They can tell you what, if anything, is worth doing next. That is their job, and it is free.

If money or card numbers have already gone out, a free legal aid office can talk with you about that as well. It is not too late to ask.

You are not in trouble for getting this email. Many people get them.
But it has a badge number and a case reference. How do you know it's not real?

That is a fair question. A badge number and a case reference look official, and they are meant to. Here is why they do not show that a letter is real.

**Anyone can type them.** A badge number in an email is just letters and numbers someone typed. There is no place you can look up "Badge #4471" to check it, because there is no office behind it. The same is true of the reference line. It carries weight only because it looks like something you have seen on real papers.

**Look at the reference itself:**

> "REF: FBE-2026-URGENT-9917"

A real case number is just a number for filing. It does not have the word "URGENT" inside it. That word is there to push you, not to file anything.

**Look at how it greets you:**

> "Dear Beneficiary,"

Your state agency and Social Security know your name, your address, and your case number. Their letters print them. This one does not know who you are.

**And the strongest sign is what it asks for.** No badge number changes this: no real office in the United States asks for gift cards, and no real office tells you to hide a letter from your caseworker and your family. Those two requests, on their own, do not belong to any real agency — no matter what name or badge sits at the bottom.

Real notices also carry things this one has no trace of: the reason for the decision, your own case number, an office address, and how to ask for a hearing.

**How you can check, rather than take my word:** the phone number printed on your own paper notices from SNAP, Medicaid, or Social Security reaches those offices. You can ask them whether anything is happening on your file. A free legal aid office can also read this email with you at no cost, and they can tell you what they see in it.

STATE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES — NOTICE OF DECISION
Date: December 8, 2026   Case: B. Example, No. 00-3390017-SN

Your SNAP application is APPROVED for the certification period December 1, 2026 through November 30, 2027.

Your monthly allotment is $0.00.

Explanation: Your household passed the eligibility test, but your net income results in a calculated allotment of zero under 7 CFR 273.10. Because you are certified as eligible, you may receive expedited processing of any reported decrease in income during your certification period, and your household remains categorically eligible for certain other assistance programs.

You must report income changes over $125.00 within 10 days. You may request a fair hearing within 90 days of the date of this notice if you disagree with the calculation. Call 555-0142.

## What this letter says

**"Your SNAP application is APPROVED for the certification period December 1, 2026 through November 30, 2027."**

They said yes to your SNAP application. This decision covers the time from December 1, 2026 through November 30, 2027.

**"Your monthly allotment is $0.00."**

Your allotment, which means the food money SNAP puts on your card each month, is $0.00. So this letter is a yes — but the monthly amount is zero.

**"Your household passed the eligibility test, but your net income results in a calculated allotment of zero under 7 CFR 273.10."**

Your household meets the rules for the program. But after the office counted your income, the monthly amount came out as zero.

**"Because you are certified as eligible, you may receive expedited processing of any reported decrease in income during your certification period, and your household remains categorically eligible for certain other assistance programs."
Approved for zero dollars?? Is this a typo? Am I approved or not?

## Am I approved or not?

I can't tell you if it is a mistake in typing. I can only tell you what the letter prints. And the letter prints both things at once:

- **"Your SNAP application is APPROVED"** — you are in the program.
- **"Your monthly allotment is $0.00."** — the food money each month is zero.

So, as printed: you are approved, and the monthly amount is zero dollars. The letter gives a reason for the zero: **"Your household passed the eligibility test, but your net income results in a calculated allotment of zero under 7 CFR 273.10."** In plain words — you meet the rules, but after the office counted your income, the monthly amount came out at zero.

The letter says being approved still means two things for you:

**"Because you are certified as eligible, you may receive expedited processing of any reported decrease in income during your certification period, and your household remains categorically eligible for certain other assistance programs."**

- If your income goes down and you tell the office, they give it expedited processing — that is, they handle it faster than usual.
- Your household is categorically eligible for some other help programs, which means being approved for SNAP can make you count as eligible for them too.

## What it asks you to do

**"You must report income changes over $125.00 within 10 days."**

You must tell the office when your income changes by more than $125.00. You must do this within 10 days.

## By when

- Income changes over $125.00: **within 10 days** of the change.
- **"You may request a fair hearing within 90 days of the date of this notice if you disagree with the calculation. Call 555-0142."** If you think the office counted wrong, you can ask for a fair hearing — a meeting where you say why you disagree. The date on this notice is December 8, 2026, and you have 90 days from that date. The number printed is 555-0142.

If you want to know whether the $0.00 is an error, a free legal aid office can look at the letter with you and help you
Then what is the point of this letter at all?

That is a fair question. Here is what the letter itself says it does, in the order it says it.

**It puts you in the program for a set time.** "Your SNAP application is APPROVED for the certification period December 1, 2026 through November 30, 2027." So for that whole year, you are in — your case is open, and you do not have to apply again to be in it.

**It sets the money at zero for now.** "Your monthly allotment is $0.00." That is today's amount, based on the income the office counted.

**It says what being in the program still gives you.** The letter names two things:
- "you may receive expedited processing of any reported decrease in income during your certification period" — if your income drops and you report it, the office handles that report faster than usual. Your allotment can be looked at again.
- "your household remains categorically eligible for certain other assistance programs" — being approved for SNAP can make you count as eligible for some other help programs.

**It tells you what you must do.** "You must report income changes over $125.00 within 10 days."

**It tells you how to disagree.** "You may request a fair hearing within 90 days of the date of this notice if you disagree with the calculation. Call 555-0142." The date on the notice is December 8, 2026.

So the letter is doing two jobs at once: it opens your case for the year, and it tells you the amount today is $0.00.

I can't tell you whether that is worth much to you — only you can weigh that. If you want someone to look at the calculation with you, a free legal aid office can do that, and the 90 days runs from December 8, 2026.
